newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Invacare rejects bid conditions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Invacare rejects bid conditions.

text.p: Invacare Corp will not drop its hostile bid for Healthdyne Technologies Inc and will not accept Healthdyne's conditions for merger talks, Invacare Chief Executive Officer Malachi Mixon said Tuesday.
He also told Reuters in a telephone interview that Invacare will try to oust the Healthdyne board at the annual shareholder meeting July 30.
"These conditions are too onerous to accept. Under these conditions, we will stay exactly where we are," Mixon said.
Mixon said he had not formally notified Healthdyne of the decision but intended to do so soon.

Healthdyne said on Monday it would talk with interested parties about a potential transaction, but it set strict conditions on talks with Invacare, including withdrawal of the suitor's $200 million takeover bid.
Healthdyne has repeatedly rejected Invacare's advances. Invacare initially launched a bid in January and has raised it three times to the current offer of $15 per share.
Although several companies have been mentioned as potential "white knights" for Healthdyne, none has come forward yet.
Shares of Healthdyne were up 1/8 to 17.
